candidates.name: Beau Bayh
candidates.gradeNote: Bayh is endorsed by the Indiana Reproductive Freedom PAC, which endorses only candidates who commit in writing to fight for access to 'safe and legal abortion.' Elsewhere he backs Indiana's voter ID law and calls for gas-tax and utility sales-tax relief, but he has stated no positions on marriage, religious liberty or guns.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Endorsed by the Indiana Reproductive Freedom PAC, which endorses only candidates who answer yes to a commitment to fight for 'access to safe and legal abortion, contraception, and fertility treatments.'
gradeJustifications.marriage: No explicit positions found on marriage, parental rights or gender issues; running as a Democrat suggests alignment with the party platform.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No positions found on religious liberty; he did not answer iVoterGuide's religious liberty questions.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No position found on gun policy; he did not answer iVoterGuide's Second Amendment question and does not appear on the 2026 Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate list for Indiana.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Says he supports Indiana's voter ID law and that only citizens should vote, but calls a push for added citizenship checks fear-mongering, and he backs citizen-led ballot initiatives, an end to straight-ticket voting and labor unions alongside cutting red tape for small businesses.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Calls for tax relief for working Hoosiers, including lowering the gas tax and eliminating the sales tax on utilities, and pledges a forensic audit of spending in the Secretary of State's office.

candidates.description: Indianapolis attorney, former U.S. Marine Corps infantry captain and son of former Gov. and Sen. Evan Bayh, nominated at the June 2026 Democratic convention.

candidates.name: Max Engling
candidates.gradeNote: Strong conservative answers on the iVoterGuide questionnaire on life, marriage, religious conscience, voter ID and voter-roll maintenance, but he has no voting or official record, and his Second Amendment and fiscal answers are general rather than specific.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Strongly agreed that life deserves legal protection from conception and that abortion providers should not receive taxpayer funds; questionnaire only, no voting record.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Strongly agreed that marriage is one man and one woman, that parents have a fundamental right to direct their children's health and education, and that transitioning a child is child abuse.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Strongly disagreed that individuals and businesses should be required to provide services that violate their religious beliefs.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Answered the gun-restrictions question only by quoting the U.S. and Indiana constitutions, without stating a specific position; not rated by NRA-PVF (which grades only federal and legislative races).
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Strongly opposes voting without photo ID, says he is cleaning ineligible voters from the rolls, opposes sanctuary cities and agreed with eliminating the U.S. Department of Education.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Proposes competitive bidding, streamlined IT and lower mailing costs for the office; no tax, spending-record or scorecard evidence found.

candidates.description: Former U.S. House Republican staffer and regional director for Sen. Jim Banks who defeated incumbent Diego Morales for the Republican nomination at the June 2026 convention.

candidates.name: Lauri A. Shillings
candidates.gradeNote: Not rated: her campaign site addresses only office administration (secure and transparent elections, simpler business filings, cutting red tape, office independence), and she did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, so there is no position on five of the six values.
candidates.description: Chair of the Hamilton County Libertarian Party and creative director at the University of Indianapolis, running as the Libertarian nominee.

candidates.name: Greg Ballard
candidates.gradeNote: As Indianapolis mayor he publicly opposed Indiana's 2015 Religious Freedom Restoration Act and urged adding sexual orientation and gender identity to state civil-rights law, and in 2014 he proposed a 43% increase in the city's public-safety income tax; no public positions on abortion or guns were found.

gradeJustifications.proLife: No position found; he did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire on abortion.
gradeJustifications.marriage: In 2015 urged lawmakers to add sexual orientation and gender identity to state anti-discrimination law.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Publicly denounced Indiana's 2015 Religious Freedom Restoration Act and asked that city ordinances be exempted from it.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No position found; he did not answer the iVoterGuide gun question and is not rated by NRA-PVF in this race.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Campaigns on independent redistricting commissions, open primaries and a nonpartisan voter guide; did not answer the iVoterGuide photo-ID question.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: As mayor proposed raising Indianapolis's public-safety income tax from 0.35% to 0.5% (approved 19-10 in 2014) to fund more police officers.

candidates.description: Former two-term Republican mayor of Indianapolis (2008-2015) and retired Marine lieutenant colonel, running as an independent on the Lincoln Party line.

candidates.name: Jessica Bailey
candidates.gradeNote: Bailey is endorsed by the Indiana Reproductive Freedom PAC, which requires a written commitment to fight for access to 'safe and legal abortion.' She also holds the 2026 Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate distinction. On fiscal issues she opposes eliminating property and gas taxes and says she would not raise taxes without serious debate.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Endorsed by the Indiana Reproductive Freedom PAC, which endorses only candidates who answer yes to a commitment to fight for 'access to safe and legal abortion, contraception, and fertility treatments.'
gradeJustifications.marriage: No explicit positions found; iVoterGuide lists an Indiana Stonewall Democrats endorsement on her profile, and running as a Democrat suggests alignment with the party platform.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No positions found on religious liberty; she did not answer iVoterGuide's religious liberty questions.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Holds the 2026 Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate distinction, which the Everytown-backed Gun Sense Voter program gives to candidates who support gun safety laws.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: No positions found on school choice or deregulation; she wants prevailing-wage and contractor standards added to the state transparency portal and is endorsed by teachers' and other labor unions, consistent with the Democratic platform.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Opposes eliminating property and gas taxes but says she would not raise taxes without serious debate, and she promises more public scrutiny of State Board of Finance transfers and an easier-to-use transparency portal.

candidates.description: Two-term Porter County Circuit Court clerk and former Portage Township school board member, running as the Democratic nominee.

candidates.name: Elise Nieshalla
candidates.gradeNote: In office she voted for a non-ESG investment policy for the state's Hoosier START retirement plan and chairs a state financial officers' national-debt task force; on the iVoterGuide questionnaire she gave consistently conservative answers on life, marriage, religious conscience, constitutional carry, parental rights and voter ID.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Strongly agreed that life deserves legal protection from conception, supports making abortion illegal with life-saving care for mother and child, and opposes taxpayer funds for abortion providers.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Strongly agreed that marriage is one man and one woman, that parents direct their children's health and education, and that transitioning a child is child abuse.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Strongly disagreed that individuals and businesses should be required to provide services that violate their religious beliefs.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Supports Indiana's constitutional carry law, with carry restrictions limited to groups such as felons, domestic abusers and the adjudicated mentally incompetent.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Strongly agreed with eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and strongly opposes voting without photo ID and sanctuary cities.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Voted in March 2025 for a non-ESG policy for a public retirement savings plan, chairs a national-debt task force with 37 state financial officers, and runs the state transparency portal and a federal-spending dashboard.

candidates.description: Incumbent Republican comptroller appointed in 2023, former Boone County Council president and former Indiana Department of Commerce economic development manager.

candidates.name: John Schick
candidates.gradeNote: Not rated: his public statements cover only the comptroller's office (independence from the governing party and a more detailed spending-transparency portal); he did not answer the 2026 surveys, and no positions on the other values were found.
candidates.description: Chesterton business consultant and former Libertarian Party state treasurer, running his third or fourth campaign for comptroller/auditor.

candidates.name: Coumba Kebe
candidates.gradeNote: Kebe is endorsed by the Indiana Reproductive Freedom PAC, which requires a written commitment to fight for access to 'safe and legal abortion.' She questions whether Indiana's anti-ESG actions, such as replacing BlackRock, served taxpayers, says a company's treatment of workers can matter to its long-term performance, and calls eliminating property taxes without a replacement plan 'an empty political promise.'

gradeJustifications.proLife: Endorsed by the Indiana Reproductive Freedom PAC, which endorses only candidates who answer yes to a commitment to fight for 'access to safe and legal abortion, contraception, and fertility treatments.'
gradeJustifications.marriage: No explicit positions found on marriage, parental rights or gender issues; running as a Democrat suggests alignment with the party platform.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No positions found on religious liberty; she did not answer iVoterGuide's religious liberty questions.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No position found on gun policy; she did not answer iVoterGuide's Second Amendment question and does not appear on the 2026 Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate list for Indiana.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Wants to use the treasurer's office to advocate for Medicaid and childcare policy changes and says government is there 'to take care of people'; no positions found on school choice or deregulation.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Says investments should maximize returns rather than make 'political and partisan statements,' but she questions whether the anti-ESG removal of BlackRock served taxpayers, says worker treatment can matter to returns, and opposes eliminating property taxes without a replacement plan.

candidates.description: Health care executive and founder of Scope Consulting, which serves home care agencies, running as the Democratic nominee after losing a Democratic primary for Indiana House District 29.

candidates.name: Daniel Elliott
candidates.gradeNote: As treasurer he put BlackRock on an ESG watchlist in 2024 and, as an INPRS board member, voted to replace it as manager of a roughly $969 million portfolio; on the iVoterGuide questionnaire he gave consistently conservative answers on life, marriage, religious conscience, guns (no new restrictions), parental rights and voter ID.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Would allow abortion only when the mother's life is in imminent danger, strongly agreed that life deserves protection from conception, and opposes taxpayer funds for abortion providers.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Strongly agreed that marriage is one man and one woman, that parents direct their children's health and education, and that transitioning a child is child abuse.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Strongly disagreed that individuals and businesses should be required to provide services that violate their religious beliefs.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Answered that no gun restrictions are needed because the constitution protects the right to keep and bear arms.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Strongly agreed with eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and strongly opposes voting without photo ID and sanctuary cities; opposes minimum-wage laws.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Placed BlackRock on an ESG watchlist, voted to replace it on a state pension portfolio, and co-founded a 37-member state financial officers' coalition on the national debt.

candidates.description: Incumbent Republican state treasurer first elected in 2022, former Morgan County Council member and software engineer/consultant.

candidates.name: Frank J. Mrvan
candidates.gradeNote: Holds an F from SBA Pro-Life America and his campaign supports codifying Roe v. Wade; he voted for the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and the 2022 Assault Weapons Ban, against the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, and scored 0% with Heritage Action in the 119th Congress.

gradeJustifications.proLife: SBA Pro-Life America grade F; campaign site says he supports the codification of Roe; voted against the 2023 Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act and did not vote on the 2025 version.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted for the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act (Roll Call 513) and against the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act (H.R. 28, Roll Call 12).
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No specific religious-liberty votes or statements found; overall voting record aligns with the Democratic platform.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Voted for the 2022 Assault Weapons Ban (H.R. 1808, Roll Call 410).
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Heritage Action 119th Congress score of 0% reflects consistent votes against that group's limited-government positions.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Heritage Action 119th Congress score of 0%; campaign emphasizes securing federal spending for the region rather than reducing it.

candidates.description: Hammond native and former North Township trustee seeking a fourth term in the U.S. House.

candidates.name: Barb Regnitz
candidates.gradeNote: A newcomer to federal office, her campaign site pledges to defend gun rights, secure the border, end reckless spending, and keep girls' sports and facilities for biological females. She has stated no position on abortion and left every iVoterGuide question unanswered. She is endorsed by President Trump, Speaker Johnson, Sens. Banks and Young, and Maggie's List.

gradeJustifications.proLife: No public position on abortion was found, and she left all of iVoterGuide's Right to Life questions unanswered; she is running as a Republican with endorsements from pro-life officeholders.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Her platform calls for 'keeping girls' sports and facilities reserved for biological females'; she has stated no position on marriage or parental rights.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No religious-liberty statements were found; iVoterGuide rates her Conservative based on public data.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Her campaign pledges to defend 'the constitutional right of law-abiding Americans to keep and bear arms without unnecessary government overreach'; she has no voting record on guns.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Campaigns on stronger border security, election-integrity measures, and supporting innovation 'without overregulation.'
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Campaigns on ending reckless spending, eliminating waste, fraud and abuse, and reducing the national debt; she has no federal record.

candidates.description: Porter County commissioner (elected 2022) with a background in software engineering and financial planning.

candidates.name: Jamee Decio
candidates.gradeNote: Has no voting record; her platform calls for eliminating ICE's budget and disbanding the agency, a pathway to citizenship and much higher taxes on billionaires. No stated positions on abortion, marriage, religious liberty or firearms were found, so those values are inferred from party alignment.

gradeJustifications.proLife: No explicit position on abortion found; running as a Democrat suggests pro-choice alignment.
gradeJustifications.marriage: No statements found on marriage, parental rights or gender issues; Democratic candidacy suggests alignment with the party platform.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No position found on religious liberty.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No position found on firearms.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Platform states 'ICE's budget should be eliminated, and the agency disbanded,' and proposes a pathway to citizenship; also calls for union labor requirements on data centers.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Calls for 'much higher taxes on billionaires' and a middle-class tax cut, and opposes coverage cuts used to fund tax breaks; would restore Medicaid funding.

candidates.description: South Bend attorney and former Elkhart County deputy prosecutor.

candidates.name: Rudy Yakym
candidates.gradeNote: Strong on life, marriage and guns (SBA Pro-Life America A+, NRA-PVF A+ and endorsed), but his fiscal and limited-government scores are good rather than top-tier: Heritage Action 85% in the 119th Congress and Club for Growth 95% for 2025 with a 78% lifetime score.

gradeJustifications.proLife: SBA Pro-Life America A+; voted for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act in 2023 and 2025.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and for the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No specific religious-liberty vote, cosponsorship or statement found beyond his vote against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Rated A+ and endorsed by NRA-PVF for 2026.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Heritage Action score of 85% in the 119th Congress; campaign pledges to cut regulations and restore federal-state balance.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Club for Growth 2025 score 95% but lifetime 78% (below its Defender threshold); Heritage Action 85%.

candidates.description: Republican who has represented Indiana's 2nd District since 2022, campaigning on limited government, lower taxes and reduced regulation.

candidates.name: William Eric Henry
candidates.gradeNote: Told the Capital Chronicle he supports any reduction in taxes at all levels and downsizing government, and favors cutting regulations that raise housing costs; no positions on abortion, marriage, religious liberty or firearms were found.

gradeJustifications.proLife: No position found.
gradeJustifications.marriage: No position found.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No position found.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No position found.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Proposes 'reducing and downsizing government' and reducing regulations and permitting delays, though he also proposes a new HUD-led home-repair partnership.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Says he supports 'any reduction in taxes in at all levels of government' and would downsize government rather than reallocate funds; no scorecard or record to confirm.

candidates.description: Elkhart communications professional and military veteran making his third Libertarian run for the 2nd District (2022, 2024, 2026).

candidates.name: Kelly Thompson
candidates.gradeNote: Lists Planned Parenthood, NOW and the ACLU among her affiliations and campaigns for Medicare for All and a new tax on Wall Street trades to fund education and erase student debt; no stated positions on firearms, marriage or religious liberty were found.

gradeJustifications.proLife: No direct statement on abortion found, but she lists Planned Parenthood and NOW among her affiliations on Ballotpedia.
gradeJustifications.marriage: No statements found on marriage or gender issues; affiliations include the ACLU and NOW, and her candidacy aligns with the Democratic platform.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No policy position found; describes a background as a visiting pastor of a jail ministry and says the Bible has most affected her life.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No position found on firearms.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Campaigns for Medicare for All and a large expansion of the federal education role, including universal pre-K and nationwide federal union negotiations for teachers.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Proposes a new 2-cent speculation tax on Wall Street trades to fund education, raise teacher pay and erase student-loan debt.

candidates.description: Concrete contractor, nonprofit founder and former jail-ministry visiting pastor from North Webster; 2020 Democratic nominee for Indiana House District 22.

candidates.name: Marlin A. Stutzman
candidates.gradeNote: Consistently top-rated: SBA Pro-Life America A+, NRA-PVF A and endorsed, Heritage Action 100% and Club for Growth 100% for 2025 (94% lifetime, ranked first); he cosponsored religious-liberty bills in his earlier House tenure and voted for a state marriage amendment in 2005.

gradeJustifications.proLife: SBA Pro-Life America A+; voted for the 2025 Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted for the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act and, as a state representative in 2005, for Indiana's one-man-one-woman marriage amendment.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Cosponsored the Marriage and Religious Freedom Act (H.R. 3133, 2013) and signed on to the First Amendment Defense Act (H.R. 2802, 2015).
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Rated A and endorsed by NRA-PVF for 2026.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Heritage Action 100% in the 119th Congress; campaign calls for finishing the border wall and says education is not a federal issue.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Club for Growth 2025 score 100% (lifetime 94%, Defender of Economic Freedom); says he authored the Conservative Congressional budget.

candidates.description: Howe farmer and business owner, former Indiana House and Senate member, who returned to Congress in 2024 after previously holding the seat.

candidates.name: Drew Cox
candidates.gradeNote: His Ballotpedia survey says he will fight to codify Roe v. Wade and pass the Equality Act, and he advocates abolishing ICE, much higher taxes on the ultra-wealthy and redirecting military spending to social programs; he also says removing the right to bear arms has no place in a free society.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Says he will fight to codify Roe v. Wade and include reproductive health care in Medicare for All.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Says he will fight to pass the Equality Act and opposes efforts to 'limit who can get married.'
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No position found on religious liberty; progressive platform including the Equality Act suggests lower priority on conscience protections.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: States that 'the removal of the right to bear arms' has no place in a free political system; no other firearm policy positions found.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Advocates abolishing ICE and passing Medicare for All, a major expansion of federal programs.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Supports the For the 99.5 Percent Act and higher tax brackets for the ultra-wealthy and corporations, and redirecting military spending to social services.

candidates.description: Purdue University music instructor and Marine Corps veteran (2008-2012) from Lafayette.

candidates.name: Jim Baird
candidates.gradeNote: Strong on life, marriage, religious liberty and guns (SBA A+, NRA-PVF A and endorsed, votes against the Equality Act and Respect for Marriage Act), but fiscal and limited-government scores are lower: Heritage Action 84% and Club for Growth 90% for 2025 with a 77% lifetime score.

gradeJustifications.proLife: SBA Pro-Life America A+; voted for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act in 2023 and 2025.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and for the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Voted against the 2021 Equality Act (H.R. 5) and the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Rated A and endorsed by NRA-PVF for 2026.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Heritage Action score of 84% in the 119th Congress.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Club for Growth 2025 score 90% but lifetime 77% (below its Defender threshold); Heritage Action 84%.

candidates.description: Farmer, small-business owner and Vietnam veteran seeking a fifth term; former Putnam County commissioner and Indiana state representative.

candidates.name: J.D. Ford
candidates.gradeNote: As a state senator, Ford voted against Indiana's 2022 abortion ban on Senate passage and again on final concurrence, after calling the bill 'extreme.' He backed the governor's veto of the 2022 girls'-sports bill, opposed the 2023 ban on gender-transition care for minors, and voted with every Senate Democrat against final passage of permitless carry in 2022. His campaign lists 'reproductive freedom,' LGBTQ+ protections and 'common sense gun policy' as priorities.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Voted against SB 1 on Senate passage (July 30, 2022) and concurrence (Aug. 5, 2022), said he would 'strongly oppose' it, and states 'I trust women to make this deeply personal decision, not the Government.'
gradeJustifications.marriage: Supported the governor's veto of HB 1041 (girls' sports), called the 2023 ban on gender-transition care for minors a ban on 'science-based healthcare,' and opposed the 2014 HJR-3 one-man-one-woman marriage amendment.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No religious-liberty-specific votes were found; iVoterGuide lists a 57% Indiana Family Institute score alongside a Liberal rating.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: All 11 Senate Democrats, including Ford, voted against final passage of permitless carry (HB 1296, 30-20, March 2022), and he lists 'common sense gun policy' as a priority.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: His platform calls for national nursing-home staffing standards and expanded federal care programs; iVoterGuide lists American Conservative Union Indiana scores of 27% and 19%.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: He cites his vote to end the sales tax on utility bills but opposed the 2025 federal reconciliation tax law as a deficit-raising giveaway to 'the billionaire class'; iVoterGuide lists a 56% NFIB Indiana score.

candidates.description: Indiana state senator for District 29 since 2018 and the first openly LGBTQ+ member of the Indiana General Assembly.

candidates.name: Victoria Spartz
candidates.gradeNote: Consistently A across values: SBA Pro-Life America A+, NRA-PVF A and endorsed, Heritage Action 92%, and Club for Growth 95% for 2025 (91% lifetime, Defender of Economic Freedom); she voted against the Equality Act and Respect for Marriage Act and against the September 2025 stopgap spending bill.

gradeJustifications.proLife: SBA Pro-Life America A+; voted for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act in 2023 and 2025.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and for the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Voted against the 2021 Equality Act (H.R. 5) and the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Rated A and endorsed by NRA-PVF for 2026.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Heritage Action score of 92% in the 119th Congress.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Club for Growth 2025 score 95% (lifetime 91%, Defender of Economic Freedom); one of two Republicans to vote against the September 2025 stopgap spending bill.

candidates.description: Republican who has represented Indiana's 5th District since 2021 and won a third term in 2024.

candidates.name: Cynthia (Cinde) Wirth
candidates.gradeNote: In a 2024 WFYI interview she said Congress should protect abortion access, calling abortion 'a health care procedure,' and called for stronger gun background checks; she also criticized diverting public-school funds to private-school programs, and her endorsements include the AFL-CIO and Progressive Voters Network.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Said she 'absolutely' would support federal abortion protections, calling abortion 'a health care procedure' that belongs between doctor and patient; a Take Back Congress profile lists 'protecting reproductive freedom' in her platform.
gradeJustifications.marriage: No statements found on marriage or gender issues; iVoterGuide rates her Liberal from public data and her candidacy aligns with the Democratic platform.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No position found on religious liberty.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Called for 'stronger background checks' and a comprehensive national system, while saying safety laws do not mean taking guns away.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Criticized 'schemes' that move money from public schools to other schools, signaling opposition to school-choice programs.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: No specific tax or spending positions found; emphasis on adequate public-school funding and progressive endorsements suggest support for higher federal spending.

candidates.description: Columbus-based small-business owner, scientist and former public high school biology teacher who was the 2024 Democratic nominee against Shreve.

candidates.name: Jefferson Shreve
candidates.gradeNote: His House record is strongly conservative: an A+ from SBA Pro-Life America, a 96% Heritage Action score, a yes vote on the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act and on H.R. 1, and a cosponsorship of national concealed-carry reciprocity. As the 2023 Indianapolis mayoral nominee, though, he proposed ending permitless carry, raising the gun-purchase age to 21 and banning assault-weapon sales, which earned an F from the NRA, so the Second Amendment grade and the overall grade stay below A.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Rated A+ by SBA Pro-Life America, which scored every one of his tracked House votes as pro-life, including the Born-Alive Act and the H.R. 1 Planned Parenthood defunding, and he cosponsored the Defund Planned Parenthood Act.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted for the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act (H.R. 28) and holds a 96% Heritage Action score; no marriage-specific vote has come before him in the House.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No religious-liberty-specific votes or statements were found; the grade rests on his 96% Heritage Action score.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: In Congress he cosponsored the Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act and campaigns on defending the Second Amendment, but in 2023 he proposed ending permitless carry, raising the purchase age to 21 and banning assault-weapon sales in Marion County, which earned an NRA 'F'.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Supported the Laken Riley Act and campaigns on securing the border; his 2023 call to let Indianapolis set its own gun rules ran against state preemption.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Voted for H.R. 1 (the 2025 reconciliation tax-and-spending law) and campaigns on cutting spending; holds a 96% Heritage Action score, with no Club for Growth rating found.

candidates.description: First-term Republican congressman, self-storage business founder and former Indianapolis City-County councilor who ran unsuccessfully for Indianapolis mayor in 2023.

candidates.name: André Carson
candidates.gradeNote: Holds an F from SBA Pro-Life America and a 0% Heritage Action score for the 119th Congress; voted for the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and Assault Weapons Ban and against the 2025 Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act and Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.

gradeJustifications.proLife: SBA Pro-Life America grade F; voted against the 2025 Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act (H.R. 21, Roll Call 27).
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted for the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act (Roll Call 513) and against the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act (H.R. 28).
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No specific religious-liberty votes or statements found; overall voting record aligns with the Democratic platform.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Voted for the 2022 Assault Weapons Ban (H.R. 1808, Roll Call 410).
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Heritage Action 119th Congress score of 0% (7% lifetime).
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Heritage Action 119th Congress score of 0% (7% lifetime).

candidates.description: Democratic congressman representing Indianapolis since a 2008 special election, Indiana's longest-serving current U.S. House member.

candidates.name: Patrick McAuley
candidates.gradeNote: McAuley has no voting record. His issues page covers only public safety, housing and job training. In a WFYI interview he called federal appropriations 'a mess' and supported voter ID, while saying he is 'completely open' to immigrants and criticizing ICE tactics. No public positions on abortion, marriage, religious liberty or guns were found.

gradeJustifications.proLife: No public position on abortion was found; he is running as a Republican, but his campaign has not addressed the issue.
gradeJustifications.marriage: No positions on marriage, parental rights or gender issues were found.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No religious-liberty statements were found.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No gun-rights position was found; on youth gun violence he favors working with local public safety officials.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Supports voter ID but says he is 'completely open' to accepting immigrants, criticized ICE tactics, and promotes federal housing programs.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Called federal appropriations 'a mess' and proposed trimming overlapping humanitarian-aid accounts, but has offered no tax or broader spending plan.

candidates.description: Republican nominee who works in commercial real estate and previously interned for U.S. Sen. Todd Young.

candidates.name: James M Sceniak
candidates.gradeNote: Sceniak calls himself pro-life but opposes abortion bans, saying abortions should be 'safe,' 'private' and 'rare.' He backs lower taxes, the Rand Paul Penny Plan, a balanced budget and returning education control to the states. He has stated no positions on marriage, religious liberty or guns.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Calls himself pro-life and opposes the death penalty, but says bans do not work, that abortions should be 'safe' and 'private,' and that medical decisions belong between patient and doctor; he would reduce abortions through contraception access and economic measures.
gradeJustifications.marriage: No position found.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No position found.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No position found; asked about school gun violence at a 2024 forum, he proposed building security such as metal detectors rather than gun restrictions.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Would return full control of education to the states, opposes federal 'one size fits all' mandates, supports a Social Security opt-out and keeping the Electoral College, and wants to end civil asset forfeiture; he also favors easier legal immigration and calls current ICE tactics unconstitutional.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Wants lower taxes for individuals, an end to deficit spending and corporate tax breaks, a balanced budget, repeal of gas taxes and the Rand Paul Penny Plan of across-the-board budget cuts.

candidates.description: Libertarian behavior therapist, Libertarian Party of Indiana vice chair and repeat candidate (2022 U.S. Senate, 2024 6th District) with no current campaign website.

candidates.name: Mary Allen
candidates.gradeNote: Allen has no federal record. Her priorities call for the ultra-wealthy and corporations to 'pay their fair share in taxes,' more USAID funding, protecting the Department of Education and universal pre-K, and she said ICE 'in its current form' needs to go away. She has stated no positions on abortion, marriage, religious liberty or guns and did not answer iVoterGuide's questions.

gradeJustifications.proLife: No explicit position on abortion was found; running as a Democrat suggests pro-choice alignment.
gradeJustifications.marriage: No explicit positions on marriage, parental rights or gender issues were found; her platform aligns with the Democratic Party.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No religious-liberty statements were found, apart from a call to let immigrant families attend religious services 'without fear.'
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No position on guns was found.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Wants to protect the Department of Education and add universal pre-K, says ICE 'in its current form' needs to go away, and calls the SAVE Act a solution to a problem that doesn't exist.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Calls for higher taxes on the ultra-wealthy and corporations and more spending on USAID, Medicaid and Medicare, while proposing to curb military spending.

candidates.description: At-large Evansville City Council member, small-business owner, Army Reserve veteran and former occupational therapist.

candidates.name: Mark Messmer
candidates.gradeNote: In the House he has an A+ from SBA Pro-Life America, a 96% Heritage Action score, and yes votes on H.R. 28 and H.R. 1. As an Indiana senator he voted against SB 1, the 2022 abortion ban, in committee and on Senate passage (26-20, July 30, 2022), saying anti-abortion groups had urged a no vote; Indiana Right to Life called that bill 'weak and troubling.' He was absent for the final concurrence vote (28-19, Aug. 5, 2022). Little direct record on guns or religious liberty keeps the overall grade at B.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Rated A+ by SBA Pro-Life America for his House votes, and he introduced the Forced Abortion Prevention and Accountability Act; his 2022 no votes on Indiana's SB 1 came after anti-abortion groups, including Indiana Right to Life, opposed that bill as too weak.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted for the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act (H.R. 28) and holds a 96% Heritage Action score; his campaign site describes him as putting faith and family first.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No religious-liberty-specific votes were reviewed; the grade rests on his 96% Heritage Action score and his self-description as an active Catholic.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No NRA rating or gun-specific votes were found for his House or state Senate service, so the grade reflects his broadly conservative record.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Describes himself as a pro-Trump conservative who believes 'less government creates more jobs' and holds a 96% Heritage Action score.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Voted for H.R. 1 (the 2025 reconciliation tax-and-spending law); no Club for Growth rating was found.

candidates.description: First-term Republican congressman from Jasper, small-business owner, and former Indiana Senate majority leader and state representative.

candidates.name: Brad A. Meyer
candidates.gradeNote: Meyer has no legislative record. He describes himself as a progressive Democrat, and his platform supports Medicare for All, a $20 federal minimum wage, stronger collective bargaining, and keeping the Department of Education; he opposes using Camp Atterbury as an ICE detention facility. He has stated no positions on abortion, marriage, religious liberty or guns and did not answer iVoterGuide's questions.

gradeJustifications.proLife: No explicit position on abortion was found; running as a progressive Democrat suggests pro-choice alignment.
gradeJustifications.marriage: No explicit positions on marriage, parental rights or gender issues were found; his platform aligns with the Democratic Party.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No religious-liberty statements were found.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No position on guns was found.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Supports Medicare for All and a $20 federal minimum wage, opposes dismantling the Department of Education, and opposes using Camp Atterbury for ICE detention.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Proposes making the first $20,000 in wages tax-free, but his agenda includes Medicare for All and 'strategic public investments' that would substantially expand federal spending.

candidates.description: Democratic nominee and Bloomington electronics engineer whose career includes manufacturing and civilian engineering work for the U.S. Navy.

candidates.name: Erin Houchin
candidates.gradeNote: Holds an A+ from SBA Pro-Life America and a 94% Heritage Action score for the 119th Congress, and voted for the 2025 Born-Alive and girls' sports bills; her Second Amendment and religious-liberty support rests on campaign pledges rather than scorecards, so under the strict standard her overall grade is B.

gradeJustifications.proLife: SBA Pro-Life America A+; introduced the Abortion Funding Awareness Act, voted to defund Planned Parenthood through H.R. 1, and voted for the 2025 Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted for the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act (H.R. 28); campaign says she voted for a Parents Bill of Rights and that parents 'should be in the driver's seat' of their children's education.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Campaign lists 'the right to worship freely' among freedoms she will defend; no religious-liberty scorecard or specific votes reviewed.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Campaign calls the Second Amendment 'one of our most important freedoms'; no NRA-PVF rating or floor votes on firearms were verified.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Heritage Action 94% (119th Congress); campaign backs finishing the border wall and cutting 'bureaucratic red tape.'
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Heritage Action 94% (119th Congress); campaign supports a Balanced Budget Amendment and tax cuts.

candidates.description: Republican congresswoman from Salem seeking a third term, a former Indiana state senator.

candidates.name: Tonya L. Hudson
candidates.gradeNote: In iVoterGuide answers she agreed life deserves legal protection from conception, opposed taxpayer funding for abortion providers, opposed any new gun restrictions and compelled services that violate beliefs, and backed abolishing the IRS and the U.S. Department of Education. She strongly disagreed with the statement defining marriage as a union of one man and one woman, though she agreed biological males should not compete in women's sports.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Agreed human life deserves legal protection from conception to natural death and strongly opposed taxpayer funding for abortion providers, but would leave the decision to 'the patient and her doctor' when lives are in danger and declined several life questions.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Strongly disagreed with the statement that marriage is a union of one man and one woman, but agreed biological males should not participate in women's sports or occupy women's spaces and supports more parental involvement in education.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Strongly disagreed that individuals and businesses should be required to provide services that violate their beliefs.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Answered 'None. See U.S. Constitution, Amendment II' on what new gun restrictions she would support.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Strongly agreed with eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and limiting federal interference in markets, but said anyone not a danger to society should be able to immigrate legally and was neutral on sanctuary cities.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Proposes abolishing the IRS in favor of a sales tax, strongly agreed with cutting spending to reduce debt, and calls a balanced budget essential.

candidates.description: Libertarian real estate broker from Mitchell who previously ran for the 9th District seat in 2020 and 2022 and for lieutenant governor.
